accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core 8.G.B.6 (explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse) and the DfE GCSE mathematics subject content (Pythagoras' theorem, G20). The rearrangement proof was rechecked by coordinates: with legs 3 and 5 the four lab triangles tile the 8 by 8 square leaving a tilted c² = 34 in picture 1 and 9 + 25 = 34 in picture 2; every rigid move keeps orientation (no reflections). Side tests recomputed: 9-12-15, 5-12-13, 7-24-25, 10-24-26 right; 6-8-11, 8-15-16, 5-6-8, 4-5-7, 3-4-6 obtuse; 4-5-6 acute (41 > 36). The adult text notes the converse is proved separately (SSS congruence).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: using the last-listed number instead of the longest side as c (13, 5, 12 test card, the 10-26-24 challenge and m2), adding sides instead of squares (7 + 24 distractor), treating a picture as proof (look distractor), circular use of a² + b² = c² inside the proof (order step blocks the conclusion line early, m8, challenge), and believing a converse is automatically true (square/rectangle example in the step text, predict and m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpproof is about proof and logical direction: rigidly sliding four congruent triangles inside one (a + b) square, ordering the lines of the area argument, sorting jobs by theorem versus converse, and judging side lists with c² against a² + b² including acute and obtuse. flagpyth (the existing Pythagoras lesson) builds squares on sides and drags corners to find lengths; none of these steps reappear. The shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner moves the triangles before the text names the result, and sees the purple c² gap become a² and b² inside an unchanged outer square; the order step only accepts the conclusion after the equal-area reason, so the learner discovers why the picture is a proof; the theorem/converse sort and the four side tests make the learner apply the converse rather than read it.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: whether the uncovered area grows, stays or shrinks when triangles slide (bigger is tempting because the gap splits), whether a true theorem proves its converse (yes is tempting), which side of 13, 5, 12 goes in c² (12, the last listed, is the trap), and whether c² > a² + b² means acute or obtuse. Each is settled by the step that follows and quoted back by A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and their own corrections: 'not 25 because 7 + 24 ≠ 25' is told to square the sides, '10² + 26² = 24²' is told c must be the longest side, 'because a² + b² = c²' is called circular, 'theorem' for the 6-8-10 corner is told it went from lengths to angle, and 'right-angled' for 5-6-8 is shown 61 ≠ 64. Lab steps also name the slip for each wrong tap (conclusion too early, missing reason, wrong bin).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs read at FK grade 1.3 and adult at 7.9 (limits 6.5 and 9.5), with one idea per paragraph: the first picture, the second picture, why the gaps match, and the converse with a worked 9-12-15 check. Precise terms are used and defined: hypotenuse, conditional statement, converse, rearrangement proof, Pythagorean triple.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with every other lesson, including Pythagoras' theorem (104), is under 12 percent. Each paragraph either builds the proof, justifies it, or applies the converse; the family tip is a concrete 30-40-50 cm corner check rather than general encouragement.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) light and dark for all six steps and after Show me: the 8 by 8 square fills the canvas width with readable triangle numbers and a² / b² labels, the four proof lines wrap inside full-width cards (shuffled order so the answer is not the layout), the job card text wraps in two lines with two large bins below, and three acute/right/obtuse zones fit across. The canvas height was trimmed (tall 1.3 to 1.15) after the first screenshots showed empty space.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every Show me finished, the challenge rendered, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark, and there were no console or page errors. Every canvas action has a button twin (Move triangle 1/3/4, each proof line, Theorem/Converse, Right-angled/Not right-angled, Acute/Right/Obtuse) and the canvas aria-label states each result, e.g. 'Sides 9, 12, 15: 9² + 12² = 225, 15² = 225. Right-angled.'
